add_retailer_version.description: Pick the date the new charges apply from. It can fall between existing versions: the next step starts from the charges in force on that date, so you only change what's different. The first version ({first}) covers every earlier period.

retailer_version.title: Retailer charges from {effective_from}
retailer_version.description: These charges apply from this date until the next version. Per-kWh values in c/kWh, ex GST.

delete_retailer_version.title: Delete retailer rate version

add_network_override.title: Override network values
add_network_override.description: Replace bundled network values from a date until the next bundled schedule takes effect, e.g. to follow what your bill charges. Per-kWh values in c/kWh, ex GST; leave a field empty to keep the bundled value. The bundled data starts on {first}.

data_description.forecast_entity: Optional. Used for the forecast price sensors.

billing.title: Billing cycle
billing.description: Meter the energy you import and export, priced at each trading period's settled price, to estimate the bill for the current cycle. Use energy meters, power sensors, or one signed grid power sensor. Energy meters must update at least every half hour; power sensors may report only when they change. Leave the meters empty to turn this off.

data_description.import_energy_entity: Energy taken from the grid: an energy meter (Wh, kWh or MWh, a running total) or a power sensor (W, kW or MW), which is integrated.
data_description.export_energy_entity: Optional. Energy sent to the grid, read the same way.
data_description.billing_cycle_day: The day of the month your bill starts on (1 to 28).
data_description.grid_power_entity: Instead of the two meters: one power sensor that is positive when importing and negative when exporting.

slow_meter.title: Energy meter reports too rarely for half-hour pricing
slow_meter.description:
In {entry}, {entity_id} reported {kwh} kWh after {minutes} minutes without a reading. Billing prices each half-hour at its own spot price, so it can only share that energy evenly over the gap, and the bill estimate is priced at the wrong half-hours.

In the entry's billing options, choose a meter that updates at least every half hour, such as an Integral helper on your grid power sensor. Daily or cloud statistics usually update too rarely.

This is flagged when a meter goes more than {limit} minutes without a reading and then reports at least {min_kwh} kWh; a gap while the meter was unavailable or Home Assistant was down doesn't count. It is cleared when the entry reloads (as choosing a different meter does) or Home Assistant restarts, and comes back if the meter still reports too rarely.
